entities.summary:
The First Epistle to the Thessalonians: A foundational text of early Christianity

Ascribed to Paul the Apostle, this New Testament epistle was written around 50 CE to address concerns and questions from the Thessalonian community. The letter addresses issues such as the return of Christ, moral behavior, and the importance of living in accordance with God's will.

This epistle played a significant role in shaping the theology and practices of early Christianity, influencing the development of Christian doctrine and practice for centuries to come.

The First Epistle to the Thessalonians is considered one of the most important texts in the New Testament, offering insights into the life and teachings of Paul and the early Christian community.
